info.name: Voice Infra — Sandbox v2 API
info.description:
The public **v2 API** for Voice Infra — outbound AI voice calls for India.

Everything you need to go from an empty workspace to a running campaign:
create an agent, place a call, watch it settle against your wallet, then dial a
whole contact list on a schedule with retries, a budget and a do-not-call list.

## Start here

1. Import `sandbox.postman_environment.json` and select the **Voice Infra — Sandbox** environment.
2. Paste your `sk_live_…` key into the `api_key` variable (it is marked secret — it is never written into the collection file).
3. Set `test_phone` to a number you own, in E.164 (`+919876543210`).
4. Work through **0-Quickstart** top to bottom. Each step stores the id the next one needs.

## Conventions

- **Base URL** — `{{base_url}}`, from the environment.
- **Auth** — `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…`, set once at the collection level. Every request inherits it.
- **Ids** — `agt_`, `call_`, `cmp_` followed by a sortable 26-character id. Treat them as opaque strings.
- **Lists** — `{data, has_more, next_cursor}`, newest first. Loop while `has_more` is true, passing `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. `limit` is 1–100, default 20.
- **Errors** — always `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`. Branch on `code`; log `message` but never parse it. `code` is an open set, so keep a default branch keyed on the HTTP status.
- **Phone numbers** — E.164 with the country code: `+919876543210`.
- **Money** — calls and the wallet are in **rupees** (`balance_inr`, `cost_inr`, `amount_inr`); campaign budgets and campaign spend are in **paise** (`budget_paise`, `spent_paise`), where **100 paise = ₹1**.
- **Times** — RFC 3339 UTC (`2026-08-10T09:16:38Z`), except campaign dates and slots, which are local to the campaign's `timezone`.

## Status and error codes

| Status | `error.code` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Fix the request; `message` names the field. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Check the key. A trailing newline from a `cat`-ed key file is the usual culprit. |
| 402 | `insufficient_balance` | Top up, then retry with the **same** `Idempotency-Key`. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The key was revoked. Nothing else returns 403. |
| 404 | `not_found` | Unknown id — including one that belongs to another workspace. |
| 409 | `conflict` | The operation is illegal in the current state. Read `status` first. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Request rate or queue depth. Honour `Retry-After` and back off. |
| 429 | `at_capacity` | All lines are busy right now. Honour `Retry-After` (30s). |
| 501 | `tier_unavailable` | The tier is published but not live. Use `t3`. |
| 502 | `upstream_error` | The carrier refused the call. Retry with backoff. |
| 503 | `campaigns_unavailable` | Campaigns are not switched on for this workspace yet — ask your account contact. |
| 503 | `fleet_offline` | No speech capacity online. Honour `Retry-After` (300s). |
| 500 | `internal` | Ours. Retry with backoff; send us the id if it persists. |

`error.code` is an **open set** — new codes appear without a version bump, so
branch on the HTTP status first and the code second. In particular, accept both
`insufficient_funds` and `insufficient_balance` on a `402`: the status is the
contract, the string is not worth a broken integration.

Retry `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, `504` and network errors with exponential
backoff and jitter. Never retry `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `501` — they fail the
same way every time. `402` is retryable only after a top-up, not on a timer.

## Limits

| Limit | Default | Over the limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request rate | 10 requests/second, burst 20 | `429 rate_limited`, `Retry-After: 1` |
| Concurrent live calls | 5 | Nothing fails — extra calls wait in `queued` |
| Queue depth (accepted, not yet ended) | 500 | `429 rate_limited`, `Retry-After: 30` |
| Contacts per campaign request | 1000 | `400 invalid_request` |
| Page size | 20 default, 100 max | Clamped |

Concurrency is a **pacer, not a gate**: over-cap calls are still accepted with 202
and dial as slots free. Only queue depth and request rate reject.

Rate and queue limits are provisioned per key. If you need more, that is a
provisioning change, not a code change — ask before the campaign, not during it.

Full reference: **https://docs.miraiminds.co**

// Surface the one-line reason on any failure, for every request.
} catch (_) { /* not a JSON error body */ }

item.name: 0-Quickstart
item.description:
Ten requests, top to bottom. Run them in order with an environment selected and
you will have created an agent, placed one real call, checked what it cost, run a
five-contact campaign end to end, and read back what was said on the call.

Each step stores the id it created in a collection variable — `{{agent_id}}`,
`{{call_id}}`, `{{campaign_id}}` — so the next step needs no copy-paste.

Before you start:

1. Select the **Voice Infra — Sandbox** environment.
2. Put your `sk_live_…` secret key in the `api_key` variable.
3. Set `test_phone` to a number you own, in E.164 (`+919876543210`). Step 2
   rings it for real and debits your wallet.

request.description:
Creates the voice agent the rest of this walkthrough uses.

`system_prompt` and `first_message` may contain `{{variable}}` placeholders; you fill them per call. The response id is saved to `{{agent_id}}`.

response.name: 201 Created

header.description: Always send this on POST /v2/calls. A retry with the same key returns the original call instead of ringing the phone twice.

request.description:
Rings `{{test_phone}}` with `{{agent_id}}`.

Answers **202 Accepted** with `{id, status}` — accepted, not yet connected. One minute at the call's tier is held from your wallet up front and reconciled when the call ends.

**Idempotency-Key** (max 255 characters, remembered for 24 hours) is what makes a retry safe. A replay comes back with the header `Idempotent-Replay: true` and the original `call_id`; no second call is placed.

response.name: 402 Wallet empty

exec: // One stable idempotency key per walkthrough run, so a retry is a replay.

request.description:
Poll until `status` is terminal: `completed`, `voicemail`, `no_answer`, `busy`, `failed`, `timeout` or `aborted`.

Polling is the fallback. In production, subscribe to webhooks instead — see the **Webhooks** folder.

request.description:
Your prepaid balance in rupees. Every call debits it when it ends; top-ups are applied by your account contact.

Poll this hourly and alert your own team below a day of traffic — a 402 mid-campaign is a worse way to find out.

A campaign dials a contact list for you inside a calling window you define, with retries and a spend cap.

It is created in `draft` — nothing rings until step 7.

`start_date` and `end_date` are filled in by a pre-request script (today and today + 7) so this request works whenever you run it. Times are local to `timezone`.

`budget_paise` is money in **paise**: 100 paise = ₹1, so `50000` is a ₹500 cap. Omit it for no cap — the wallet is still the hard limit.

exec: // Keep the calling window valid whenever this collection is run.

request.description:
Moves the campaign to `play` and begins dialling inside the next open slot. **202 Accepted**.

If the wallet cannot cover every remaining contact the campaign still starts and the response carries `funded_calls` — how many calls the current balance pays for. The campaign dials those, then pauses itself with `pause_reason: "insufficient_balance"`.

exec: console.warn("balance covers only", r.funded_calls, "calls — top up to finish the list");

request.description:
The campaign object plus live `counters` — contacts grouped by status (`pending`, `claimed`, `dialing`, `completed`, `voicemail`, `no_answer`, `busy`, `failed`, `timeout`, `exhausted`, `suppressed`, `aborted`).

`spent_paise` is money already billed, in paise.

query.description: Add `format=csv` for the per-contact CSV export.

request.description:
Roll-up for the campaign: contacts, dial attempts, connections and spend.

`connected` counts calls that reached a person or a machine (`completed` + `voicemail` + `timeout`). `spent_paise` is authoritative; `spent_inr` is the same number in rupees for convenience.

Add `?format=csv` for one row per contact — see the **Campaigns** folder.

What was actually said on the call from step 2, turn by turn.

This is the point of the whole walkthrough: you now have a call you can read, audio you can play (**Get recording**), and — if the agent was created with `analysis.enabled` — a summary on the call object itself.

**404** here means the call has not ended yet, or nobody spoke. Poll step 3 until `transcript_available` is `true`.

response.name: 200 OK
404 Call has not ended yet

item.name: Agents
item.description:
An agent is a reusable configuration: prompt, opening line, voice, language and
call limits. Calls and campaigns reference one by id.

Ceilings enforced on create and update: `system_prompt` 8,000 characters,
`first_message` 500 characters, `max_duration_secs` 30–1800 (default 300).

`voice` is an **object** — `"voice": "ashutosh"` is rejected — and
`voice.voice_id` is a slug drawn from the catalogue of the **tier** the agent
runs on. On `t3`, the default tier, the default voice is `ashutosh`. On
`t1` the catalogue is exactly two: `ashu` (the default there) and `aishe`.
A slug from outside the tier's catalogue is refused at write time with
**400 `invalid_request`**, rather than failing inside the synthesiser with
the customer already on the line.

**About `{{customer_name}}` in the prompts below.** Those are *agent* placeholders,
filled by the platform from each call's `variables` — they are not Postman
variables. Postman leaves an undefined `{{…}}` untouched, so they reach the API
intact. Just do not define a Postman variable with the same name, or Postman will
substitute it before we ever see it.

**`analysis`** is optional and off unless you ask for it. With
`{"enabled": true}` every call this agent runs is read once after it ends and
the call object gains `{summary, success, data}`. Add `analysis.prompt`
(up to 2,000 characters) to say what you want pulled out of the conversation —
the answer lands in `analysis.data`. Analysis never delays a call, never
delays its webhook, and a failure leaves `analysis: null` rather than
retrying.

request.description:
**201 Created** with the full agent object.

Required: `name`, `system_prompt`, `first_message`, `voice.voice_id`, `language`.
Optional: `max_duration_secs`, `end_call`, `voicemail`.

response.name: 201 Created

request.description: Newest first. Deleted agents are omitted.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: An id that belongs to someone else answers **404**, exactly like an id that never existed. That is deliberate — a 403 would confirm the id is real.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Send only the fields you are changing.

Nested objects (`voice`, `end_call`, `voicemail`) are **replaced whole**, not merged — send every key you want to keep. Calls already running are unaffected.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: **204 No Content**. The agent stops appearing in lists and can no longer start new calls; calls already in flight finish normally and past calls keep resolving their `agent_id`.

item.name: Calls
item.description:
One outbound call. `POST /v2/calls` answers **202 Accepted** — the request was
accepted, the phone has not rung yet.

**Money.** Rates are per minute, rounded up, one-minute minimum. Tier `t3` —
the default — is ₹3/minute (300 paise); tier `t1` is ₹1/minute (100 paise).
One minute is held from the wallet when the call is accepted and reconciled
against the real duration when it ends; unbilled endings
(`no_answer`, `busy`, `failed`, an abort before answer) release the hold in
full and report `cost_inr: null`.

**Statuses.** `queued` → `dialing` → `in_progress` → one of `completed`,
`voicemail`, `no_answer`, `busy`, `failed`, `timeout`, `aborted`. Terminal
statuses never change.

**Phone numbers** are E.164 with the country code: `+919876543210`.

**After the call.** Every ended call carries `recording_available` and
`transcript_available`. When they are true, `GET /v2/calls/{id}/transcript`
returns the turns and `GET /v2/calls/{id}/recording` redirects to a signed
15-minute URL for the audio. Both are kept for 90 days. Agents created with
`analysis.enabled` also get an `analysis` object on the call — a summary, a
success flag, and whatever you asked for in `analysis.prompt`.

header.description: Up to 255 characters, remembered for 24 hours. Always send one.

request.description:
Places one call. **202 Accepted** with `{id, status: "queued"}`.

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent_id` | yes | Must exist in your workspace. |
| `to` | yes | E.164, e.g. `+919876543210`. |
| `variables` | no | Flat string map, at most 32 keys, 512 characters per value. |
| `webhook_url` | no | HTTPS, public host. |
| `max_duration_secs` | no | 30–1800. Overrides the agent for this call. |
| `tier` | no | Defaults to your key's tier, `t3` (₹3/minute). Pass `t1` for the ₹1/minute tier — a `t1` call needs an agent whose `voice.voice_id` is `ashu` or `aishe`. |

**Idempotency.** Send `Idempotency-Key` on every attempt. A retry with the same key returns the original response with `Idempotent-Replay: true` — no second call is placed. A timeout tells you nothing about whether the phone rang; the key is what makes the retry safe.

**Over capacity.** Past your queue depth you get `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. Being merely at your concurrency ceiling does not fail — those calls wait in `queued` and dial as slots free.

originalRequest.description: The same call placed on `t1` instead of the default `t3`. `t1` bills ₹1/minute against ₹3, and its voices are `ashu` and `aishe` — so the `agent_id` you send must be an agent created with one of those two, not the `ashutosh` agent the quickstart builds.

response.name: 402 Insufficient balance
429 Queue full
400 Bad phone number

request.description:
The call object.

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | See the folder description. |
| `ended_reason` | Why it ended — `customer-ended-call`, `assistant-ended-call`, `customer-did-not-answer`, `exceeded-max-duration`, `voicemail`, … `null` while running. Treat as an open vocabulary. |
| `duration_secs` | Seconds of live audio. `null` until the call ends. |
| `cost_inr` | Rupees charged. `null` means nothing was charged. |
| `started_at` | Set when audio goes live, not when we dialled. `null` if never answered. |
| `recording_available` | `true` once the call's audio is stored. Fetch it from **Get recording**. |
| `transcript_available` | `true` once the call produced speech. Fetch it from **Get transcript**. |
| `analysis` | `{summary, success, data}` — only for agents created with `analysis.enabled: true`. `null` otherwise, and `null` while the call is still running. |

The two `*_available` booleans exist so you do not have to fetch a transcript to find out whether there is one. Both are `false` until the call ends.

request.description:
What was said, as turns, once the call has ended.

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `role` | `assistant` or `user`. Nothing else appears — internal notes and tool steps are not conversation. |
| `text` | The turn as spoken. Hindi, Hinglish and English arrive as they were said; nothing is translated. |
| `start_ms`, `end_ms` | Milliseconds from the start of the **recording**, so a turn lines up with the audio from **Get recording**. `end_ms` can be `null` on the last turn of a call that was cut off. |

**404 while the call is still running**, and **404 for a call that produced no speech at all** (nobody answered, or the line was silent). Check `transcript_available` on the call first if you want to tell those apart from a mistyped id.

Transcripts are kept for 90 days, the same as the call record itself.

response.name: 200 OK
404 Not available yet

request.description:
**302** to a signed, time-limited URL for the call's audio (WAV). Follow the redirect — most HTTP clients do by default; `curl` needs `-L`.

The signed link is valid for **15 minutes**. It is a way to fetch this recording now, not a permanent URL: do not store it, store the `call_id` and ask again. Anyone holding the link can fetch the audio until it expires, so treat it as you would the recording itself.

**404** while the call is running, for a call that produced no audio, and for a call whose audio was never stored. `recording_available` on the call object tells you which requests are worth making.

response.name: 404 No recording

exec: pm.test("302 or 200 after following the redirect", () =>

request.description:
Cancels a call that is `queued`, `dialing` or `in_progress`. **202 Accepted**, then the call settles as `aborted`.

A call aborted before it was answered is not billed. One that had already connected is billed for the time it ran.

Aborting a call that has already ended answers **409 conflict** — read `status` first.

item.name: Campaigns
item.description:
A campaign dials a contact list for you: it respects a calling window, paces
itself to a concurrency you choose, retries the ones that did not connect, skips
anything on your do-not-call list, and stops at a budget.

**Lifecycle.** `draft` → `play` → (`paused` ⇄ `play`) → `completed` or
`stopped`. Only `play` dials. `stopped` and `completed` are terminal.

**Editing.** `PATCH` works on `draft` and `paused` campaigns only — pause first
if you need to change a running one. New contacts can be added to a running
campaign; a `stopped` or `completed` one refuses them, because nothing would
ever dial them.

**Money is in paise.** 100 paise = ₹1. `budget_paise: 50000` is a ₹500 cap;
`spent_paise` is what has actually been billed. Omit `budget_paise` for no cap —
your wallet is still the hard limit.

**Bounds** (rejected with `400 invalid_request` outside these):

| Field | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | 1–120 characters | — |
| `slots` | 1–4 windows, `HH:MM` | — |
| `max_concurrent` | 1–50 | 1 |
| `retry_count` | 0–5 (retries after the first attempt) | 0 |
| `re_attempt_period_secs` | 60–86400 | 900 |
| `max_duration_secs` | 30–1800 | the agent's value |
| `contacts` per request | up to 1000 rows | — |

**`503 campaigns_unavailable`** means campaigns are not switched on for this
workspace yet — ask your account contact, it is a provisioning step, not a bug in
your request.

request.description:
Creates a campaign in `draft` and loads its first contacts in the same request. **201 Created**.

Required: `name`, `agent_id`, `timezone` (IANA, e.g. `Asia/Kolkata`), `start_date`, `end_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive, local to `timezone`), `slots`.

**The response is the campaign object itself** — every field `GET /v2/campaigns/{id}` returns, at the top level — plus `contacts_accepted`, `contacts_duplicate` and `contacts_rejected`. There is no wrapper to unwrap.

**Bad rows do not fail the batch.** `contacts_rejected` is always an array (never `null`) and names each bad row by its **index** in your list, with the `reason` it was refused, so you can fix them without diffing your own file. A request only fails outright if it carries more than 1000 rows.

Contact `id` is yours — pass your own CRM id and it comes back in the report. Omit it and one is assigned.

response.name: 201 Created — two rows rejected

  "pause_reason": null,
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "start_date": "2026-08-11",

request.description:
One row per contact.

| `pending` | Waiting for a slot. |
| `claimed` / `dialing` | Being dialled now. |
| `completed` `voicemail` `timeout` `no_answer` `busy` `failed` | The last call's outcome. |
| `exhausted` | Retried up to `retry_count` and never connected. |
| `suppressed` | On your do-not-call list. |
| `aborted` | The campaign was stopped while this contact was in flight. |

`last_call_id` joins the row to `GET /v2/calls/{id}` for the transcript-level detail.

Starts (or resumes) dialling. **202 Accepted** with `{id, status: "play"}`.

Before starting, the platform checks that speech capacity is online and estimates whether your wallet covers the remaining contacts. If it does not, the campaign still starts and the response adds `funded_calls` — the number of calls the current balance pays for. It dials those and pauses itself with `pause_reason: "insufficient_balance"`; top up and start it again.

Starting a campaign that is already `play`, `stopped` or `completed` answers **409**.

response.name: 503 No capacity online

request.description: Stops dialling new contacts; calls already connected finish. **202 Accepted**. Only a `play` campaign can be paused. A paused campaign can be edited, then resumed.

response.name: 409 Not running

request.description:
Picks a paused campaign back up. **202 Accepted**.

If the campaign has been paused long enough that nothing is holding its place, resume answers **409** and names the fix: call `/start` instead, which re-runs the wallet and capacity checks a bare resume would skip.

response.name: 409 Use start instead

request.description: Ends the campaign for good. **202 Accepted**. Works from `draft`, `play` or `paused`; `stopped` is terminal and the campaign cannot be restarted or given new contacts. Use pause if you might want it back.

The roll-up.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `contacts` | Rows in the campaign. |
| `dialed` | Contacts with at least one attempt. |
| `attempts` | Total dial attempts, retries included. |
| `connected` | Reached a person or a machine (`completed` + `voicemail` + `timeout`). |
| `spent_paise` | Billed so far, in paise (100 paise = ₹1). |
| `spent_inr` | The same amount in rupees. |
| `budget_paise` | Your cap, or `null` if uncapped. |

One row per contact, streamed as a download named `<campaign_id>.csv`.

Columns: `id`, `phone`, `status`, `attempts`, `last_call_id`. `id` is your own contact id when you supplied one, so this joins straight back to your CRM.

item.name: DNC
item.description:
Your workspace's do-not-call list. Any number on it is skipped by every campaign
in the workspace and the contact is marked `suppressed` in the report.

This is **your** suppression list, not a national registry. Scrubbing against the
national DND/NCPR list, keeping consent records and honouring an opt-out spoken
on a call remain your obligations as the business placing the calls.

Add a number the moment someone opts out — during a call, by SMS, by email,
anywhere.

request.description:
**201 Created** the first time (`added: true`), **200 OK** if it was already there (`added: false`). Adding the same number twice is not an error — you got what you asked for.

E.164 only: `+919876543210`.

response.name: 400 Not E.164

request.description: Newest first, `{data, has_more, next_cursor}`.

**204 No Content** on removal, **404** if the number was not listed. URL-encode the leading `+` as `%2B` if your client does not do it for you.

Removing a number means you have fresh consent to call it. Keep the record.

response.name: 404 Not listed

item.name: Wallet
item.description:
Voice Infra is prepaid: one INR wallet per workspace. Calls debit it as they end;
top-ups are applied by your account contact.

**Units.** The wallet and the call ledger are in **rupees** (`balance_inr`,
`amount_inr`, `cost_inr`). Campaign budgets and campaign spend are in **paise**
(`budget_paise`, `spent_paise`) — 100 paise = ₹1. Nothing in the API mixes the
two inside one object.

**Rate.** Tier `t3` — the default — bills ₹3 per minute (300 paise); tier
`t1` bills ₹1 per minute (100 paise). Both round up, with a one-minute
minimum. Calls that never connect are not billed at all.

request.description:
`balance_inr` is spendable rupees and is never negative. `updated_at` is when it last moved.

A call reserves one minute at accept time, so the balance drops the moment you place a call and is reconciled — refunded or topped up to the real cost — when the call ends.

The ledger, newest first. One row per credit or debit.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | `credit` (top-up) or `debit` (a call). |
| `amount_inr` | Rupees moved. |
| `balance_after_inr` | Balance once this row was applied. |
| `call_id` | The call this row paid for, or `null` for a top-up. |

Reconcile by summing `amount_inr` where `type` is `debit` — not by differencing balances.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description:
Webhooks are how you learn what happened. Polling is the fallback, not the design.

Pass `webhook_url` when you create a **call** or a **campaign** and we POST a
signed JSON event at each lifecycle transition. Your endpoint must be public
HTTPS and must return any `2xx` quickly.

**Nothing in this folder calls the Voice Infra API** — these items document the
contract and let you fire a correctly signed test delivery at your own endpoint.

## Event types

Call events (`webhook_url` on `POST /v2/calls`):

| Type | Fires when | `data.call.status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `call.queued` | Accepted, waiting to dial. | `queued` |
| `call.started` | Audio is live, the conversation has begun. | `in_progress` |
| `call.completed` | Connected and finished normally. | `completed` |
| `call.voicemail` | An answering machine picked up. | `voicemail` |
| `call.failed` | Did not connect, or the call errored. | `no_answer`, `busy`, `failed` |
| `call.aborted` | You cancelled it. | `aborted` |

Exactly one terminal call event fires per call.

Campaign events (`webhook_url` on `POST /v2/campaigns`):

| Type | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `campaign.started` | The campaign began dialling. |
| `campaign.paused` | Paused — by you, or by the platform (see `pause_reason`). |
| `campaign.resumed` | Dialling picked back up. |
| `campaign.completed` | Every contact reached a final state. |
| `campaign.stopped` | You ended it. |

Campaign events are **one per lifecycle transition, not one per call**. A 50,000-
contact campaign that posted an event per call would flood your own endpoint; the
per-call events are already available on the call webhook if you want them.

## Envelope

Both families share one envelope — `{id, type, created_at, data}`. Call events
carry `data.call`; campaign events carry `data.campaign`.

Treat the envelope as additive: new fields appear without a version bump, so
ignore what you do not recognise, and always have a default branch on `type`.

## Signature

Every delivery carries this header:

```
X-Mirai-Signature: t=1786440000,v1=771bca27e1647dfbe59ff5d8f32d9de69be246f6e604c05bddcbaefd8604ccb3
```

- `t` — Unix seconds at signing time.
- `v1` — lowercase hex **HMAC-SHA256** over the exact string `"<t>" + "." + <raw request body>`, keyed with your workspace's `whsec_…` secret (issued with your API key).

Verify in four steps:

1. Parse `t` and `v1` out of the header.
2. Reject if `|now − t| > 300` seconds.
3. Recompute the HMAC over `t + "." + raw_body`.
4. Compare in **constant time**.

```javascript
import crypto from "node:crypto";

export function verify(rawBody, header, secret) {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(
    header.split(",").map((p) => {
      const i = p.indexOf("=");
      return [p.slice(0, i).trim(), p.slice(i + 1).trim()];
    })
  );
  const { t, v1 } = parts;
  if (!t || !v1) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(t)) > 300) return false;   // replay window

  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${t}.`)
    .update(rawBody)          // the RAW bytes, never a re-serialised object
    .digest("hex");

  const a = Buffer.from(expected, "utf8");
  const b = Buffer.from(v1, "utf8");
  return a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}
```

```python
import hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(raw_body: bytes, header: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    parts = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in header.split(","))
    t, v1 = parts.get("t"), parts.get("v1")
    if not t or not v1:
        return False
    if abs(time.time() - int(t)) > 300:          # replay window
        return False
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{t}.".encode() + raw_body,
                        hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, v1)
```

**The single most common integration bug** is signing a re-serialised body. Capture
the raw bytes before any JSON parser touches them: `express.raw({ type: "application/json" })`
in Express, `request.body` in Django, `request.raw_post` in Rails.

## Retries, ordering and dead-letter

- A delivery succeeds on any `2xx`. Anything else — `4xx`, `5xx`, timeout, TLS or DNS failure — is retried: **six attempts with exponential backoff over roughly 36 minutes**, the first immediately, gaps widening to a half-hour cap.
- After the sixth attempt the event goes to a **dead-letter queue**. It can be replayed for you on request: a replayed event is byte-identical, **including its `id`**, and carries a fresh `t`/`v1` so it still passes your replay window.
- **Order is not guaranteed.** A retried `call.started` can arrive after `call.completed`. Drive your state machine off `data.call.status`, not off arrival order.
- **Slow endpoints are retried.** If your handler is slower than our client timeout we treat it as a failure. Acknowledge first, do the work after.
- **Assume at-least-once delivery.** Dedupe on the event `id` with a TTL longer than the retry window (24 hours is comfortable), or make your handler naturally idempotent.
- A `401` from your own signature check counts as a retryable failure to us — deliberately, so a transient secret-loading bug on your side does not lose the event.

## Checklist

- [ ] Public HTTPS endpoint that returns 2xx in well under a second.
- [ ] Signature verified against the **raw** body, in constant time.
- [ ] Replay window enforced at 300 seconds.
- [ ] Events deduped on `id`.
- [ ] Unknown `type` values ignored, not crashed on.
- [ ] No slow work inline — enqueue and return.

item.name: Send a signed test event to your endpoint (call.completed)

request.description:
Fires a **correctly signed** sample `call.completed` delivery at your own endpoint, so you can test your receiver before burning wallet balance on a real call.

Set two environment variables first:

- `webhook_endpoint` — your receiver, e.g. `https://example.com/mirai/webhook`
- `webhook_secret` — the `whsec_…` issued with your API key

The pre-request script signs the exact body bytes the way the platform does — `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")` — and puts the header value in `{{webhook_signature}}`. If your handler accepts this, it will accept the real thing.

This request does **not** touch the Voice Infra API and sends no credentials.

exec: // Sign the request body exactly as the platform does:
console.warn("set webhook_secret (your whsec_…) before sending this");

item.name: Send a signed test event to your endpoint (campaign.paused)

request.description:
The campaign flavour of the same envelope: `data.campaign` instead of `data.call`, same header, same signature scheme, same 300-second replay window — one verification code path covers both.

`pause_reason` appears only when the platform paused the campaign itself: `insufficient_balance` (wallet ran dry) or `budget_exhausted` (`budget_paise` reached). A pause you requested carries no reason.

Uses the same `webhook_endpoint` and `webhook_secret` variables as the previous request.
